s: Which is the nodal department responsible to coordinate disaster management in India?
x: The Ministry of Home Affairs is the nodal ministry for disaster management in India (except for drought, pest attack and epidemics).

s: The first Disaster Management Training Institution of the country is being established at:
x: The first Disaster Management Training Institute of the country has been established in Latur, Maharashtra by the CRPF. Since Nagpur is not given in the options, the question is based on the institute set up by the CRPF.

s: On which river and at which place did scientific flood forecasting in India begin in 1958?
x: It began in 1958 on the Yamuna at Delhi under the then Central Water & Power Commission.

s: Who chaired the High Powered Committee on Disaster Management (1999)?
x: The High Powered Committee on Disaster Management constituted in 1999 was chaired by J. C. Pant.

s: Under which ministry was the Disaster Management Cell, set up in the 1990s in response to the UN IDNDR, placed?
x: In the 1990s, a Disaster Management Cell was established under the Ministry of Agriculture in response to the UN International Decade for Natural Disaster Reduction.

s: In which year was India's first National Disaster Management Plan (NDMP) issued?
x: The first NDMP came in 2016 and was revised in 2019 in alignment with the Sendai Framework.

s: In which year was the National Centre for Disaster Management at IIPA set up?
x: The NCDM was set up in 1995, before the DM Act (2005), the National Policy (2009) and the Sendai Framework (2015).

s: The High Powered Committee on Disaster Management (1999) grouped disasters into how many broad categories?
x: The High Powered Committee, set up in 1999 under J. C. Pant, classified disasters into five broad categories.

s: What was the theme of the High Powered Committee Report?
x: The HPC theme 'Building a Culture of Prevention' marked a shift from relief to prevention, mitigation and preparedness.

s: Which was the first state in India to establish a dedicated Ministry of Disaster Management?
x: Uttarakhand was the first State with a separate disaster management ministry; DM moved from Agriculture to Home Affairs in 2002.

s: What did the original mandate of the 1999 High Powered Committee cover?
x: The HPC first covered only natural disasters; its mandate was later widened to man-made disasters.

s: In which year did the Gujarat earthquake that led to the Ministry of Home Affairs becoming nodal for disaster management occur?
x: The Gujarat earthquake was in 2001, followed by the tsunami (2004) and the DM Act (2005).

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: NDRF – Policy body chaired by the Prime Minister
NDMA – Chaired by the Union Home Secretary
National Executive Committee – Operational control through NDMA
x: NIDM is the capacity-building institute under MHA; the NDMA is the PM-chaired policy body, the NDRF works under NDMA control and the NEC is chaired by the Home Secretary.

s: The change in Andhra Pradesh’s disaster-management approach is described as a shift from:
o: A mitigation-centric approach to a relief-centric approach
A district-centric approach to a village-centric approach only
A warning-based approach to a compensation-only approach
A relief-centric approach to a mitigation-centric approach
x: Andhra Pradesh has moved from a relief-centric approach towards a mitigation-centric approach and is regarded as a national leader in disaster-risk reduction.

s: Which event exposed gaps in India's disaster response and led to the enactment of the Disaster Management Act, 2005?
x: The DM Act followed the gaps exposed by the 2004 tsunami, and it extends to the whole of India.

s: In which year were the Andhra Pradesh Disaster Management Rules, under which APSDMA is chaired by the Chief Minister, made?
x: The Andhra Pradesh Disaster Management Rules were made in 2007.

s: Which of the following correctly represents the three Ps in the post-2005 disaster management approach?
x: The post-2005 '3 Ps' are prevention, preparedness and proofing (mitigation). The old '3 Rs' were rescue, relief and rehabilitation.

s: In pursuance of which law was the National Policy on Disaster Management (NPDM) formulated?
x: The NPDM was framed under the DM Act, 2005 and moved from relief to prevention and preparedness.

s: Where was the first India Disaster Management Congress (November 2006) held?
x: NIDM organised the first India Disaster Management Congress in New Delhi in November 2006.

s: Where is the Disaster Management Institute, set up in 1987 after the gas tragedy, located?
x: The Disaster Management Institute, Bhopal was set up in 1987 after the Bhopal gas tragedy.

s: In which year was disaster management shifted from the Ministry of Agriculture to the Ministry of Home Affairs?
x: The subject moved from Agriculture to Home Affairs in 2002, after the 2001 Gujarat earthquake.

s: Where was the Central Emergency Relief Training Institute (CERTI), India's first disaster management training institution, set up in 1957?
x: CERTI was set up at Nagpur in 1957 as India's first disaster management training institution.

s: Which was the first disaster management training institution of India?
o: National Institute of Disaster Management, New Delhi
Central Emergency Relief Training Institute, Nagpur
National Centre for Disaster Management, IIPA
x: CERTI, Nagpur (1957) came first; DMI Bhopal (1987), NCDM (1995) and NIDM (2003) came later.

s: Which is the nodal ministry for air accident disasters?
The Disaster Management Act was enacted in:
x: The DM Act (Act No. 53) received Presidential assent on 23 December 2005, so it was enacted in 2005. The 2006 date relates to NDMA's notification and NDRF's raising, not the Act.

s: Which Chapter of the Disaster Management Act 2005, mentions about District Disaster Management Authority?
x: Section 25 on the DDMA falls in Chapter IV of the DM Act, so Chapter IV is correct.

s: District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) is headed by
o: Any of them as the case may be
x: The District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) is headed by district collector or district magistrate. Thus district Disaster Management Authority in Jharkhand is headed by the District Magistrate or District Collector. So, option (c) is the correct answer.

s: Section ....... of the Disaster Management Act, 2005 empowers Governor of a State to establish a State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA).
x: Section 14(I) of the Disaster Management Act, 2005 empowers Governor of a State to establish State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA). In each state, after the notification under Section 3(1) of this Act, the Governor shall establish the State Disaster Management Authority.

s: Hazard-specific plans of the Union ministries are prepared under which Section of the DM Act, 2005?
x: Hazard-specific plans fall under Section 35 and Ministry DM Plans under Section 37; Section 25 concerns the DDMA.

s: In which year was the Disaster Management Act, 2005 most recently amended?
x: The DM Act was amended in 2025, updating definitions such as risk and resilience.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Disaster Management (Amendment) Act, 2025?
o: It creates national and state disaster databases.
It gives statutory status to the National Crisis Management Committee.
Urban Disaster Management Authorities are headed by the Mayor.
It makes a State Disaster Response Force mandatory in every state.
x: Under the 2025 amendment a UDMA is headed by the Municipal Commissioner, not the Mayor; the other three are features of the amendment.

s: By whom is the State Disaster Management Authority established under Section 14?
x: The Governor sets up the SDMA under Section 14, and the Chief Minister chairs it.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: NIDM is associated with Section 42. Section 44 deals with the National Disaster Response Force.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about disaster management funds?
o: The National and State Disaster Response Funds are meant for relief.
The National and State Disaster Mitigation Funds are meant mainly for post-disaster relief.
NDRF may refer both to a response force and to a response fund.
The National and State Disaster Response Funds are distinct from the mitigation funds.
x: The mitigation funds are meant for mitigation; relief is supported by the response funds.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Section 46 relates to the National Disaster Response Fund, whereas the National Disaster Mitigation Fund is provided under Section 47.

s: How many Chapters and Sections does the Disaster Management Act, 2005 contain?
x: The DM Act has 11 chapters and 79 sections.

s: The National Disaster Response Fund has its legal basis in which Section of the DM Act, 2005?
x: Section 46 provides for the National Disaster Response Fund and Section 48 for the State fund; Sections 14 and 25 set up the SDMA and DDMA.

s: With whom does the primary responsibility for disaster management in India lie?
x: States have primary responsibility; the Centre, through MHA, provides support, coordination and resources.

s: NDMA's 'Resilient India 2047' asks for Ministry Disaster Management Plans under which Section of the DM Act?
x: It asks for hazard-specific plans under Section 35 and Ministry DM Plans under Section 37; Sections 46 and 48 are the response funds.

s: The National Institute of Disaster Management is provided for under which Section of the DM Act, 2005?
x: Section 42 provides for NIDM; s.44 is the NDRF force, s.46 the NDRF fund and s.25 the DDMA.

s: The National Disaster Response Force is constituted under which Section of the DM Act, 2005?
x: The NDRF force is under s.44; the National Disaster Response Fund is under s.46.

s: The National Executive Committee is constituted under which Section of the DM Act, 2005?
x: s.8 creates the NEC; s.3 the NDMA, s.14 the SDMA and s.25 the DDMA.

s: Under the DM (Amendment) Act, 2025, who heads an Urban Disaster Management Authority?
x: A UDMA is headed by the Municipal Commissioner; UDMAs cover Municipal Corporation cities except Delhi and Chandigarh.

s: Which of the following statements about the NDRF is incorrect?
o: The legal basis of the NDRF is Section 44 of the Disaster Management Act, 2005.
The NDRF functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
x: Option A is incorrect: the NDRF was raised in 2006 under Section 44 of the DM Act, 2005. 2005 is the year of the Act, not the force.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: State Disaster Response Force – Trained by the NDRF or NDRF Academy
State Disaster Response Fund – Legal basis is Section 48(1)(a)
State Executive Committee – Administers the State Disaster Response Fund
State-specific disasters – Up to 25% of SDRF may be used
x: Only up to 10% (not 25%) of the SDRF may be used for State-specific disasters. The SDRF (fund) rests on Section 48(1)(a), the State Executive Committee administers it, and the State Disaster Response Force is trained by the NDRF/NDRF Academy.

s: On which date did the Disaster Management Act, 2005 receive Presidential assent?
x: The DM Act (Act No. 53 of 2005) received Presidential assent on 23 December 2005.

s: What is the Act number of the Disaster Management Act, 2005?
x: The Disaster Management Act is Act No. 53 of 2005; it has 11 Chapters and 79 Sections.

s: Under which Section of the DM Act, 2005 is the District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) constituted?
x: Section 25 (Chapter IV) provides for the DDMA; Section 14 is for the SDMA and Section 8 for the NEC.

s: For which of the following is the Ministry of Home Affairs NOT the nodal ministry under India's disaster management set-up?
x: MHA is the nodal ministry for disaster management except for drought, pest attack and epidemics.

s: Under the DM (Amendment) Act, 2025, Urban Disaster Management Authorities are set up in Municipal Corporation cities except in which places?
x: UDMAs are set up in Municipal Corporation cities and State capitals, except Delhi and Chandigarh.

s: Which decade did the UN declare as the International Decade for Natural Disaster Reduction (IDNDR)?

s: Which of the following is NOT a major activity in the pre-disaster stage of the Disaster Management cycle?

s: With which of the following is CAP-SACHET associated?
x: CAP-SACHET is used for early warning dissemination, a preparedness measure like mock drills and stockpiling.

s: Compensation and psychosocial care are measures of which phase of the disaster management cycle?
x: Compensation and psychosocial care are recovery measures; response includes restoring critical services.

s: Regulating deforestation is a measure of which phase of disaster management?
x: Prevention, which is proactive and long-term, includes controlling deforestation.

s: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of the response phase of disaster management?
x: Response is time-critical; being a long-term activity describes recovery.

s: Which one of the following is a PRE-DISASTER mitigation measure?
x: Retrofitting is undertaken before a disaster to strengthen existing structures and reduce potential damage. Damage assessment, compensation and psychosocial care belong to the post-disaster phase.

s: Against which hazard is planting trees along coastal areas a mitigation measure?
x: Coastal tree belts reduce cyclone damage; awareness and education are non-structural mitigation.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The community is usually the first responder.
The Collector plays a pivotal role in disaster response.
The fire brigade alone has the basic responsibility for urban response.
The district administration has the basic responsibility in urban response.
x: Option C is incorrect: urban response is shared by civic bodies, the fire brigade and police, with the district administration in overall charge. The community is usually the first responder.

s: Which of the following represents the correct post-disaster management sequence?
x: After a disaster comes relief, then restoration, then reconstruction and finally resilient rebuilding.

s: Which phase of disaster management aims to restore normal life and reduce future vulnerability?
x: Recovery aims to bring back normal life and lower future vulnerability through rehabilitation and reconstruction. Response is the immediate action, and mitigation reduces impact beforehand.

s: Of which phase of disaster management are land-use zoning and control of industrial siting measures?
x: Prevention covers land-use zoning and industrial siting; mitigation covers quake-proof buildings and hazard maps.

s: Emergency Operation Centres and contingency plans are tools of which phase?
x: Emergency operation centres and contingency plans are preparedness tools.

s: Which phase of disaster management is considered the most cost-effective?
x: Mitigation reduces a disaster's impact in advance, which costs less than relief and rebuilding later.

s: Recovery, with its focus on building back better, belongs to which stage of disaster management?
x: Recovery is the post-disaster stage; prevention, mitigation and preparedness come before, and response during, a disaster.

s: Which phase, concerned with being ready before a disaster occurs, is called the first and critical step in disaster management?
x: Preparedness is called the first critical step because it is about being ready before a disaster strikes.

s: Why is the disaster management cycle continuous?
o: Lessons from recovery lead to better prevention
x: The cycle is continuous since lessons from recovery feed into better prevention.

s: Mitigation belongs to which phase of the Disaster Management Cycle?
x: The pre-disaster phase is made up of prevention, mitigation and preparedness.

s: In GIS applications across the disaster management cycle, to which phase does evacuation route planning belong?
x: Evacuation route planning is preparedness; hazard zonation is prevention and real-time damage assessment is response.

x: Mock drills, Aapda Mitra volunteers and tsunami escape-route signage are preparedness tools; entering flowing floodwater is unsafe and is not a preparedness measure.

s: A sudden recession of the sea, requiring immediate movement inland or uphill, may come before which disaster?
x: A sudden sea recession may precede a tsunami, which is why immediate inland or uphill movement is advised.

s: In the colour-coded warning system of the India Meteorological Department, what does the colour ORANGE indicate?
x: Green means all well, yellow means be aware, orange means be prepared and red means take action.

s: Which of the following safety actions is NOT correctly recommended?
o: During a flood, avoid walking or driving through flowing water.
During a flood, move to higher ground.
During a cyclone warning, stand under a large tree until the storm passes.
Indoors during an earthquake, drop, cover and hold under a strong table away from windows.
x: During a cyclone one must move to a cyclone shelter or safer building and never stand under trees.

s: In which month and year was India's first disaster management exercise on forest fires held in Uttarakhand?
x: The first forest-fire disaster management exercise was held in Uttarakhand in April 2017.

s: Which award did Uttarakhand's Disaster Mitigation & Management Centre win in 2020?
o: Subhash Chandra Bose Aapda Prabandhan Puraskar
x: Uttarakhand's Disaster Mitigation & Management Centre won the Subhash Chandra Bose Aapda Prabandhan Puraskar 2020.

s: Which command conducted 'Prakampana', the super-cyclone preparedness exercise at Visakhapatnam?
x: Prakampana was a super-cyclone preparedness exercise at Visakhapatnam by the Eastern Naval Command with civil agencies.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's Tsunami Ready programme:
1. India aims to make 100 villages Tsunami Ready.
2. Recognition is renewed every 4 years.
3. The recognition board is chaired by the Director of IMD.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: India targets 100 Tsunami Ready villages, renewed every 4 years; the board is chaired by the Director, INCOIS, not IMD.

s: Which is the nodal agency for landslide hazard zonation, susceptibility maps and the Landslide Atlas?
x: The Geological Survey of India is the nodal agency for landslide hazard zonation, susceptibility mapping and the Landslide Atlas.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Damini App provides lightning alerts. The other pairs assign disaster-management tools to unrelated functions.

s: Under which mission was IMD's Multi-Hazard Early Warning Decision Support System (MHEW-DSS) launched in 2024?
x: MHEW-DSS is a webGIS platform launched by IMD in 2024 under Mission Mausam, reaching about 80% of the population.

s: In which year was the Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre at INCOIS, Hyderabad established?
x: The ITEWC at INCOIS was set up in 2007 and issues alerts within about 10 minutes.

s: Which is the technical agency for earthquakes in India?
x: The National Centre for Seismology (MoES) handles earthquakes; IMD handles cyclones, INCOIS tsunamis and CWC floods.

s: Which agency issues storm surge and high-wave warnings in India?
x: INCOIS warns of storm surge and high waves; IMD forecasts, tracks and names cyclones.

s: Which institution runs India's earthquake early-warning pilot in Uttarakhand?
x: IIT Roorkee runs the earthquake early-warning pilot in Uttarakhand; the National Centre for Seismology (MoES) is the earthquake agency.

s: About which hazard does IMD's Damini app give warnings?
x: IMD's Damini app is for lightning; tsunamis are with INCOIS, landslides with GSI and river floods with CWC.

s: Which centre forecasts and names cyclones over the North Indian Ocean?
x: IMD's Regional Specialised Meteorological Centre (RSMC), New Delhi forecasts, tracks and names North Indian Ocean cyclones.

s: Which app of the National Centre for Seismology gives earthquake information?
x: The NCS (MoES) runs the IndiaQuake app; Damini is IMD's lightning app.

s: Where was India's indigenous GLOF alert system tested?
x: An indigenous glacial lake outburst flood alert was tested at Sissu in Himachal Pradesh.

s: On what basis does Landslide Hazard Zonation divide hill areas into homogeneous zones?
o: Degree of susceptibility, hazard or risk
x: Zoning is based on the degree of susceptibility, hazard or risk; such maps are probabilistic, not certain predictions.

s: Why is Google Earth Engine particularly useful in disaster management?
o: Processes large satellite-image archives for rapid flood mapping
Operates India’s network of cyclone shelters
Issues statutory evacuation orders to district authorities
x: Google Earth Engine is a cloud platform that processes extensive satellite-image archives and can support rapid flood mapping.

s: Which organisation maintains the National Database for Emergency Management (NDEM), a GIS repository for the disaster management cycle?
x: NDEM is maintained by ISRO, not IMD.

s: Storm surge modelling with GIS is used mainly for which hazard?
x: GIS models storm surges for cyclones; for floods it maps inundation and for droughts it supports NADAMS.

s: For what are INSAT-3D/3DR satellites mainly used in disaster management?
x: INSAT-3D/3DR are used to track cyclones.

s: For which hazard is NADAMS used in India?
x: NADAMS (National Agricultural Drought Assessment and Monitoring System) is the GIS/remote-sensing tool for drought.

s: Which body runs the State Emergency Operations Centre of Andhra Pradesh?
x: APSDMA runs the State Emergency Operations Centre, coordinates districts, operates early warnings and plans restoration.

s: Near which place did Cyclone Michaung (December 2023) make landfall in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Michaung made landfall near Bapatla; Hudhud hit Visakhapatnam in October 2014.

s: About how many Bay of Bengal low-pressure systems affect Andhra Pradesh annually?
x: AP is associated with 13–14 such systems a year, mostly from the northern Bay, which can flood the Godavari and Krishna basins.

s: Which body operates the alert systems Vajrapath, Varuna and Red Message?
x: APSDMA issues State-level alerts and runs systems such as Vajrapath, Varuna and Red Message.

s: Which set lists cyclone risk-reduction measures used in Andhra Pradesh?
o: IMD warnings, cyclone shelters, evacuation, shelter belts and mangroves
x: Cyclone risk reduction includes IMD warnings, shelters, evacuation, shelter belts and mangrove protection or restoration.

s: Where did Cyclone Hudhud (October 2014) make landfall?
x: Hudhud struck Visakhapatnam in 2014; Titli came near Palasa (2018) and Michaung near Bapatla (2023).

s: Which of the following pairs (cyclone – landfall) is correctly matched?
x: Titli (2018) made landfall near Palasa in Srikakulam; Hudhud hit Visakhapatnam and Michaung came near Bapatla.
